title: Ball a release height
description: Essential: Correctly calculates h_a = 1.25 m from energy conservation and the condition for circular motion at D.

title: Ball b release height (part 2)
description: Essential: Correctly calculates h_b = 1.0625 m (17/16 m) using energy conservation and the electric force condition at C.

title: Ball b release height (part 3)
description: Essential: Correctly calculates h_b' = 2.13 m (32/15 m) using energy conservation and the projectile motion condition for vertical impact.

title: Energy conservation application
description: Important: Applies the work-energy theorem correctly, accounting for gravitational potential energy and, for ball b, electric potential energy.

title: Force condition at top
description: Important: For ball a at D, sets net centripetal force equal to mg. For ball b at C, sets centripetal force equal to electric force Eq.

title: Projectile motion analysis
description: Important: For part 3, correctly derives the relationship v_D / (g t) = tan(53°) from the condition of vertical impact on the slope.

title: Geometric displacement relation
description: Optional: For part 3, correctly relates the horizontal displacement from D to the vertical drop using the slope angle (x/y = 8/3).

title: Sign error in electric work
description: Pitfall: Uses incorrect sign for the work done by the electric field in the work-energy theorem for the charged ball.

title: Centripetal force misconception
description: Pitfall: For ball a at D, incorrectly includes normal force or other forces in the centripetal force condition (mg = mv²/R).
